objective: Classify triple common neighborhoods, derive the exact one-star boundary relation, and give a minimum boundary obstruction with a genuine cubic realization.

atomic_claims.text: A triple has a common neighbor exactly when its distinct labels are pairwise nonadjacent; the nonzero cardinalities are 5, 2 and 1.
One-star repair with a fixed exterior is possible exactly when its exterior-label set does not totally dominate B.
Four distinct exterior labels are the minimum obstruction; a four-element target set totally dominates B exactly when it induces C4.
An eight-vertex triangle-free subcubic tree is a vertex-minimum failure witness for the stated degree-three-center one-star rule.
A 48-vertex connected planar triangle-free cubic graph has a homomorphism on G-v that cannot be repaired on N[v], while G itself also has a homomorphism.

assumptions: Finite simple triangle-free subcubic source; degree-three center; exterior labels are fixed.
The initial map is a genuine homomorphism on all of G-v.
Use the exact B and generator relation from C02/C06; empty intersections and repeated labels have explicit semantics.
risks: All mathematical arguments are paper candidates; no solver, enumeration or kernel execution.
The cubic witness has bridges; it does not defeat a separately restricted 3-edge-connected repair rule.
Failure of a prescribed partial map is not graph-level nonexistence.
The eight-vertex minimum is for the stated subcubic repair rule, not for cubic root counterexamples.

failed_route_proposal.blocker: Only the auxiliary universal one-star repair rule fails. The admitted five-transversal equivalence route remains active. Sections 5-6 give explicit failures with actual maps on G-v and separate maps of G.
